title: Modified Staff-ball Technique for Densely Vegetated Areas
protocol: Locate a dimensionless-point target at the center of a circle.
Position the point target at the intersection of the upper arc of a tennis ball with 7 cm diameter and the right or left side of a vertical staff.
Mount the tennis ball on a vertical staff.
Place the point targets in randomly chosen points within the plots, typically in bushes.
Use two 2m PVC pipes cut into two pieces and joined by connectors for easier transportation.
Set up one pipe as the viewing pole and another where the tennis ball is kept.
Ensure the sight distance from the target to the observer's eye is four meters.
Place the point targets at a specific height of 1.25 m above ground level.
Observe this non-dimensional point from equally-spaced points systematically distributed in the circle.
Align observations correctly to minimize errors caused by vegetation obstructing sight lines.
Take 15° angle deviation away from the normal using a protractor and 2 m pole.
Deviate 15° towards the point target, forming an inverted V shape.
Sight each observation with one eye to avoid parallax error.
Assume a stationary posture before viewing the target.
Adjust the height of the eye according to marks on the staff-pole held by the observer.
Consider all six observations within the circle as a single observation.
Calculate percent cover by dividing the number of points where the target is not visible by the total number of points along the circumference, then multiplying by 100.
